title: Prefetch Heatmap Pilot & Rollout Playbook for Adaptive Serving
creator: Ariadne Gomez
description: Objective: Reduce per-token unit costs for conversational workloads by selectively prefetching KV cache segments and enabling heatmap-driven batching without violating latency SLOs. This playbook covers the pilot (50-customer sandbox), canary rollout, and full rollout phases. Key results: 1) 8-12% token cost reduction for mid-length conversations (seq len 512–2048) under production mix, 2) <5% p95 tail increase in token latency, 3) no customer-facing quality regressions detected by the eval suite. Scope: prefetch heuristic + heatmap telemetry, server-side scoring service for prefetch decisions, small inference runtime hook for safe KV prefetch, and a control-plane rollout config exposed in Console for canary groups.
acceptance_criteria: Automated heatmap scoring service running in staging and returning decisions within 2ms median
Field experiment shows >=8% token cost savings in at least 3 of 4 target buckets
No increase in model output regression alerts tied to our canonical eval prompt set
Console toggle exists for 'Prefetch Heatmap' with per-customer opt-in and audit logs
milestones: M2: Scoring service prototype + integration tests (2026-03-01)
M3: Staging pilot with 5 internal apps (2026-03-14)
updates: 2026-02-05: Kickoff completed. PM aligned with research and infra on target KRs. Initial instrumentation schema approved.
2026-02-18: Heatmap ingestion pipeline merged; sampling rate set to 0.5% to limit steady-state overhead. ENG requested an opt-out header for internal traffic.
2026-03-01: Scoring service prototype returns decisions at 1.8ms median in local perf tests. Quant team flagged potential memory pressure when prefetch window > 8 segments.
2026-03-10: Staging pilot with 5 internal apps running. One app observed a 0.7% p95 latency increase; we reduced prefetch aggressiveness for that app and created a per-route override.
2026-03-14: Decision to gate aggressive prefetching behind a runtime knob and Console canary flag. Field trial targeting configuration finalized.
decision_log: Trade-off: Aggressive prefetch yields higher savings but increased memory and tail latency. Decision: adopt conservative default (prefetch top-2 heatmap segments) and provide a graded knob (0-3) for power users.

Trade-off: Run scoring service as sidecar vs centralized microservice. Chosen: centralized scoring service to simplify rollout and collect global heatmaps; added local fallback logic to avoid cross-service latency amplification.

Security: Prefetch telemetry contains no customer PII; we will still route telemetry through KMS-wrapped transport and redact request_ids in logs. Security review deemed required for on-prem deployments; request opened with SecOps.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Memory pressure on older GPU instances when prefetching many KV segments. Mitigation: soft-limit per-device prefetch window and fall back to non-prefetch path when memory headroom < 15%.
Risk: Quality regressions due to stale cache prefetch. Mitigation: conservative heuristics, immediate validation pipeline comparing outputs with and without prefetch for a replayed prompt set.
Risk: Unexpected customer opt-outs leading to fragmented telemetry. Mitigation: track opt-out rate and complement with synthetic canary traffic to ensure coverage.
